Showkat Ahmad Joo vs Ut Of J&K Through Financial ... on 4 
April, 2024 
Author: Rahul Bharti
Bench: Rahul Bharti
 High Court Of Jammu & Kashmir And Ladakh
 At Srinagar
 Reserved on : 02.04.2024.
 Pronounced on : 04.04.2024.
Case:- WP(Crl) No. 265/2023
Showkat Ahmad Joo,
Aged about 35 years,
S/o Farooq Ahmad Joo,
R/o Green Colony Wuyan Pampore,
District Pulwama (Detenue)
Through his father
Farooq Ahmad Joo
Aged about 57 years,
S/o Abdul Aziz Joo
R/o Green Colony Wuyan Pampore,
District Pulwama
 ....Appellant(s)/Petitioner(s)
 Through: Mr. Syed Sajad Geelani, Advocate
 Vs
1 . Ut of J&K through Financial Commissioner, 
 (Addl. Chief Secretary) Home Department, J&K Jammu/ Srinagar. 
2. District Magistrate Pulwama, Kashmir
 ..... Respondent(s)
 Through: Mr. Zahid Qaiz Noor, Ga
Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Rahul Bharti, Judge
 Judgment
01. Heard the learned counsel for both sides. Perused the writ pleadings and the record therewith. 
02. The respondent No. 2 - District Magistrate, Pulwama has subjected the petitioner to preventive detention custody by virtue of an Order dated 34/DMP/PSA/23 dated 24.05.2023 in order to prevent the petitioner from acting in a manner prejudicial to the security of the State and upon his Showkat Ahmad Joo vs Ut Of J&K Through Financial ... on 4 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23252072/
1 detention to be kept in Central Jail Kot Bhalwal, Jammu. 
03. It is the Sr. Superintendent of Police (SSP), Awantipora, who vide his letter No.
Conf/PSA/2023/457-60 dated 15.05.2023, submitted a dossier against the petitioner to the respondent No. 2 - District Magistrate, Pulwama thereby making out a case for preventive detention of the petitioner. The dossier related the petitioner to be a person in contact with various separatists and other fringe elements under whose influence the petitioner had become a radical and fundamentalist, acting as a provider of all possible assistance like food, shelter, finance,
transportation besides acting as a courier of classified information regarding statement of movement of police and security forces to the Lashker-e-Toiba (LeT) and The Resistance Front (TRF).
04. The petitioner's implication in FIR No. 84/2012 under Section 13 of Unlawful Activities (Prevention), Act, 1967 with the Police Station Tral, which is pending criminal trial in the criminal court was cited to confirm the alleged profile of the petitioner. The petitioner is alleged to have been apprehended on 02.05.2023 in terms of Section 107/151 of Cr. P.C. and came to be released by furnishing of bond before the Executive Magistrate Ist Class, Pampore. The petitioner is alleged to have been again arrested on 11.05.2023 by same mode of legal action under Section 107/151 Cr. P.C.
and again to be released after execution of a bond before the Executive Magistrate Ist Class,
Pampore.
05. It is with this backdrop that third time, instead of resorting to Section 107/151 Cr. P.C., the preventive detention under the J&K Public Safety Act, 1978 came to be applied against the petitioner by the respondent No. 2-District Magistrate, Pulwama. It is this detention order which is in serious challenge in the writ petition. 
06. A bare perusal of the grounds of detention supporting the preventive detention order would show that from Section 107/151 Cr.P.C. the respondent No. 2 - District Magistrate, Pulwama switched over to the J&K Public Safety Act, 1978 without first enquiring and confirming the fact that as to whether the petitioner's bond as well of his sureties' bond submitted in the proceedings under Section 107/151 Cr.P.C before the Executive Magistrate Ist Class, Pampore were ever forfeited or not because if the petitioner was continuing with his alleged state of activities which had led to his booking under Section 107/151 Cr.P.C, obviously at that point of time the petitioner's alleged state of activities were not of that potential which in the estimate of the district Police as well of the Executive Magistrate concerned admitted of preventive detention option against the petitioner and if that is so then in case if the petitioner is allegedly reported to have re-lapsed into his objectionable activities for refraining from which the petitioner had executed a personal bond as well as surety bonds under Section 107/151 Cr.P.C., before the Executive Magistrate Ist Class, Pampore, then first thing which ought to have happened at the instance of the district Police stepping forward to seek preventive detention of the petitioner is the forfeiture of the personal as well as surety bonds by applying to the Magistrate concerned, but that seems to have least bothered the district Police as well as the respondent No. 2 - District Magistrate, Pulwama and, therefore, the drastic measure of preventive detention of the petitioner came to be resorted which renders the impugned detention order of the petitioner ex-facie illegal and warrants it to be set aside, notwithstanding the approval/
Showkat Ahmad Joo vs Ut Of J&K Through Financial ... on 4 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23252072/
2 confirmation by the Govt. of UT of Jammu & Kashmir based upon the opinion report of the Advisory Board.
07. In view of the aforesaid, the impugned detention Order No. 34/DMP/PSA/23 dated 24.05.2023 against the petitioner is hereby set aside and the petitioner is to be set free to his personal liberty by the Superintendent of the Jail concerned with immediate effect.
08. Disposed of accordingly. 
09. Detention record is returned back. 
(RAHUL BHARTI) JUDGE SRINAGAR 04.04.2024.
